causes.label: Low-value amounts
causes.description: The attack never moved an amount large enough to stand out. Every transaction sat inside the band ordinary customers occupy.
causes.remediation: Score cumulative value over 7-30 day windows, not just per-transaction amount. Add sub-threshold-repetition features.

causes.label: Merchant mimicry
causes.description: Cash-out went through merchants the victim already used, or through an aged merchant record, so acceptance-side signals stayed clean.
causes.remediation: Track per-customer-per-merchant amount distributions, not just whether the pair has been seen before.

causes.label: Aged synthetic identity
causes.description: A fabricated identity that had already accumulated enough account age and clean history to look established.
causes.remediation: Verify against authoritative sources at origination; footprint consistency beats behavioural history for thin files.

causes.label: Slow / patient pacing
causes.description: Events were spaced far enough apart that no velocity window ever saw them together.
causes.remediation: Add long-horizon velocity (7d/30d) and per-account risk state that decays over days rather than resetting every 24 hours.

causes.label: Familiar geography
causes.description: Ran from the victim's usual location, defeating distance and impossible-travel checks.
causes.remediation: Do not treat home geography as exculpatory; weight it lower when other context is anomalous.

causes.label: Low velocity footprint
causes.description: Transaction counts stayed inside normal daily rhythm; no burst or fan-out was visible in any short window.
causes.remediation: Aggregate across the campaign, not the account-hour.

causes.label: Visible only as a sequence
causes.description: Individually unremarkable events whose only incriminating property is their ordering — invisible to per-row scoring.
causes.remediation: Sequence model over the account timeline, plus beneficiary in-degree graph features.

causes.label: Familiar device
causes.description: Executed from a device already established on the account, so device-novelty signals never fired.
causes.remediation: Behavioural-biometric continuity within the session; detect device-familiar but behaviour-anomalous activity.

causes.label: Existing beneficiary
causes.description: Value was routed to a payee already on file, so new-payee controls and cooling-off windows did not apply.
causes.remediation: Monitor dormant-payee reactivation and sudden step-changes in amount to a long-standing payee.

causes.label: No credential trace
causes.description: No password change, profile edit or failed-login burst preceded the fraud, so account-compromise heuristics had nothing to fire on.
causes.remediation: Cover the authorised-push-payment case explicitly: fraud where nothing is compromised needs intent signals, not auth signals.

moves.rationale: Detector misses attacks whose amounts sit inside the victim's normal range, so compress the drain toward that range and take the value in more, smaller pieces.
Acceptance-side novelty is being caught, so cash out through merchants the victim already transacts with.
Origination signals are weak against aged fabricated identities, so invest in a longer cultivation period.
Velocity windows never see the events together, so widen the inter-event gaps and stretch the campaign across more days.

meta.methodology: Before and after are evaluated on the SAME adversarial batch, generated independently of the batch used for retraining, at a matched false-positive budget.
